en: Victory be unto you, O Lord of the Gaṇas; grant me vast intelligence, and bestow upon me constant inspiration to perform your hymn of praise day and night. || 1 ||
Even Candra and Indra meditate upon you, the Lord who is the embodiment of auspiciousness; Viṣṇu and Śiva worship you and always meditate upon you, the Imperishable One.
They call you Vināyaka, the elephant-faced bestower of auspiciousness; by your name, O destroyer of the impurities of the Kali age, all defects go to their dissolution.
Marked by your lotus feet, I bow at your feet; you are the Lord of Gods and the One-Tusked One (Gajāsura); O Lord, hear my petition. || 4 ||
Show me affection, protect me as you would all [your devotees]; protect me constantly from obstacles and perform all my rites for me.
O Gaṇeśa, son of Gaurī, listen to my petition; seeking no other goal than your feet, I beg you for the protection of all my interests.
You alone are my mother and father; you are my imperishable God. You are the protector of the helpless; O All-pervading Lord, grant me the fruit I desire.
You are the pot-bellied one, the elephant-faced Lord Siddhivināyaka; you are Heramba, the son of Śiva, the Lord of Obstacles, and the kinsman of the helpless.
O elephant-faced one, protector of devotees, you who grant boons, have mercy! You are the color of vermilion, holding an axe in your hand, the destroyer of obstacles.
People have sung of you as the one worthy of trust, the Lord of auspiciousness, the Lord of obstacles, the wielder of the axe, the enemy of evil, the kinsman of the distressed, and the Lord of all.
I bow to the remover of obstacles; I salute the illustrious Lord of the Pramathas. I bow to the one with a single tusk, and I pay homage to the kinsman of the distressed. 11.
Salutations to the son of Śambhu; salutations to the abode of compassion. Homage be to you, O Gaṇeśa; and homage be to you, O Lord.
Homage be to the King of the Gods; I again salute the Son of Gaurī. With devotion, I bow at the feet of Bhālacandra and Gaṇeśa.
There is no hope whatsoever in my heart for devotion to you or for your praise; rather, there is only one hope in my heart: that I may behold you.
Ignorant and deluded as I am, I meditate upon your feet; grant me your vision quickly, O Lord of the Universe, and show me mercy. 15.
I am but a child and of little knowledge, yet you are the Lord of all; O Gajānana, you are the protector of all your devotees. (16)
"I am poor and devoid of fortune; may my mind be fixed upon your feet. O compassionate one, grant a vision of yourself to me, who have no other refuge. (17)
Whoever recites this hymn to Gaṇapati with a well-concentrated mind shall, through the grace of Gaṇeśa, obtain the perfection of knowledge and wealth. (18)
The devoted person who, having worshipped the deity, recites this hymn that bestows success, shall never be afflicted by the torment of spirits, ghosts, and the like. (19)

Whoever, having recited it, praises this hymn to Siddhivināyaka, attains success within six months; these words shall not be false. Having bowed at the feet of Gaṇeśa, the devotee Divākara speaks thus. (20)
